title: Stream of Characters
spaceBreakdown:
- Trie nodes: up to 2000 × 200 = 4×10⁵ nodes, each with 26 pointers + 1 bool → O(N × L)
- string buffer: capped at maxLen ≤ 200 characters → O(L)
- No recursion, no auxiliary containers
- Not counted: input words vector
approach: Build a trie of the **reversed** words. This transforms suffix matching into prefix matching: a suffix of the stream matches a word iff the reversed suffix is a prefix of some reversed word. Maintain a rolling buffer of the last `maxLen` stream characters (at most 200). On each query, append the new character, then walk the trie from the newest character backward. Return true the moment any trie node along the walk is a word-end; return false if a child is missing or the buffer is exhausted without a match.
hints: When you need to check if a *suffix* of the stream equals a word, what single transformation on the words turns every suffix check into a prefix check? The longest word is at most 200 characters.

Build a **trie of the reversed words**. For `words = ["cd","f","kl"]` the trie is root→d→c(end), root→f(end), root→l→k(end). Keep a buffer of the last 200 stream chars and walk the trie backward from the newest character.

```
build trie of reversed words
maxLen = longest word length
buffer = empty

query(letter):
    append letter to buffer
    trim buffer to last maxLen chars
    node = root
    for i from buffer.end down to buffer.start:
        if node has no child for buffer[i]: return false
        node = child
        if node is word-end: return true
    return false
```

**Not reversing words** - words inserted forward, trie checks prefixes instead of suffixes
`StreamChecker(["cd"])`, queries `'c'`, `'d'` → `[false, true]`
⚠️ Bug: inserting "cd" forward as root→c→d(end), walking from buffer end → on query `'d'`, buffer="cd", root has no child `'d'`, returns `false`

**Stopping at non-end node** - returning false when current node is not a word end
`StreamChecker(["ba"])`, queries `'b'`, `'a'` → `[false, true]`
⚠️ Bug: `if (!cur->isEnd) return false` after advancing → on query `'a'`, buffer="ba", root→a is not an end, returns `false` instead of continuing to root→a→b

**Only checking end at walk completion** - not checking isEnd at each step
`StreamChecker(["a", "cba"])`, queries `'b'`, `'a'` → `[false, true]`
⚠️ Bug: checking `cur->isEnd` only after the for loop → on query `'a'`, buffer="ba", walks root→a→b, loop ends at non-end node, returns `false` (misses shorter word "a")

**Popping wrong end of buffer** - losing newest characters instead of oldest
`StreamChecker(["cd"])`, queries `'a'`, `'b'`, `'c'`, `'d'` → `[false, false, false, true]`
⚠️ Bug: `buffer.pop_back()` instead of `buffer.erase(buffer.begin())` → on query `'d'`, buffer becomes "abc", walks from 'c': root has no child 'c' (reversed "dc" → root→d→c), returns `false`

followUps.q: Support dynamic insertion of new words during streaming - how does the approach change?
followUps.a: Insert each new word reversed into the existing trie in O(L) time. Update `maxLen` if the new word is longer. The buffer and query logic remain identical. TC per insertion: O(L); per query: O(L).

followUps.q: Return the longest matching suffix instead of a boolean - what changes?
followUps.a: Instead of returning true at the first word-end, continue walking the entire buffer and track the deepest end node reached. Return the corresponding word (store the original word at each end node during trie construction). TC unchanged: O(L) per query.

followUps.q: If memory is extremely limited and the trie is too large, what alternative works?
followUps.a: Replace the trie with a hash set of all reversed words. On each query, check every suffix length 1..maxLen of the reversed buffer against the set. TC: O(L²) per query (L ≤ 200, so 40 000 ops), SC: O(N × L) for the set but with smaller constant factor than 26-pointer trie nodes.
